problem_type: Project graph operations and history restore do not preserve complete ownership
symptom: Cross-layer copy/move throws, asset undo leaves entries behind, duplicated layers lose track order, nested ungroup detaches children, and switching entities retains stale clip selection. Cross-parent grouping, cloning and crowd creation detach local coordinates; malformed saved parent cycles hide the object tree.
direct_cause: Cross-layer writes capture a frozen target outside the draft; history restores a hand-picked field list; graph edits ignore parent and track references; selection pruning validates IDs globally instead of against their selected owner.
class_root: User actions are treated as partial field mutations rather than complete project and owned-subtree transactions.
affected_population: Objects, groups, cameras and lights crossing scenes
Nested groups and copied scene track ordering
All clip and keyframe selection owners

external_sources.purpose: Confirm transform composition and the non-uniform parent-scale limitation of TRS reparenting.

invariants: A composite action creates one reversible history entry and rolls back on error
All project writes use the live draft
Subtrees retain internal references and track metadata
A selected clip/keyframe belongs to the selected entity
Reparenting and cross-layer transfer transform rest poses and every trajectory in the same coordinate frame
Loaded parent graphs are rooted forests
generality_proof: The store owns complete snapshot restoration and action grouping for all callers; cross-scene operations resolve both scenes inside the same draft; shared selection pruning validates ownership after every project mutation and selection change.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Complete project history, grouped actions and owned selection pruning.
Move/copy a complete entity subtree inside one project draft.
Shared affine-space and subtree semantics for grouping, ungrouping, clone and scene transfer.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Both save project history; complete restore now includes assets.
Controls dispatch to draft-bound transfer and owner-aware selection.
Compound user actions consume withHistory and restore as one action.

recurrence.reason: The same operations are reachable for every project and entity family, and missing snapshot fields recur when project schema grows.
same_class_scan: Read asset actions and camera/timeline composed actions
Checked scene duplication and remapSceneIds track references

prevention.invariant: Complete project history and owner-aware selection are enforced at the store boundary.
prevention.failure_mode: Invalid targets are rejected before mutation and failed compound actions restore their original state.
prevention.strategy: Replace partial snapshot field restoration and captured frozen writes with complete grouped project operations.

legacy_paths.rationale: Remove partial history restoration, frozen target writes and globally-valid but wrongly-owned selection.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: Existing immutable draft and project types are sufficient; no runtime upgrade controls these application invariants.

migration: No schema change. Existing projects are normalized and future copy/move/history operations use the corrected shared boundary.
residual_risks: Non-uniform parent scale combined with rotation can create shear that the existing TRS schema cannot represent exactly; no new shear schema is introduced.
Physical-phone sensors and external AI service are outside the project graph tests.

invariant_owner_layer.why: 不变量由 src/workbench/generationCanvas/nodes/director/model/directorStore.ts 单点持有（即本合同的 prevention.enforcement_path / shared_boundaries）；上游其它入口只调用它、不各自重判。tests 是该层现有的类级与回归测试，改动这条不变量必先让它们红。
